{{Infobox probability distribution|name=''κ''-Erlang distribution|type=density|parameters=<math> 0 \leq \kappa < 1 </math> <br /> <math> n =  \textrm{positive} \,\,\textrm{integer}   </math>|support=<math>x \in [0, +\infty)</math>|pdf=<math>   \prod_{m = 0}^n \left[ 1 + (2m -n)\kappa \right] \frac{ x^{n - 1} }{ (n - 1)! }  \exp_\kappa(-x)  </math>|cdf=<math> \frac{1}{ (n - 1)! } \prod_{m = 0}^n \left[ 1 + (2m -n)\kappa \right] \int_0^x z^{n - 1} \exp_\kappa(-z) dz  </math>|pdf_image=FILE:Kaniadakis Erlang Distribution pdf.png|pdf_caption=Plot of the κ-Erlang distribution for typical κ-values and n=1, 2,3. The case κ=0 corresponds to the ordinary Erlang distribution.}}

The '''Kaniadakis Erlang distribution''' (or '''κ-Erlang Gamma distribution''') is a family of [[Probability distribution|continuous statistical distributions]], which is a particular case of the [[Kaniadakis Gamma distribution|κ-Gamma distribution]], when <math>\alpha = 1</math> and <math>\nu = n = </math> positive integer.<ref name=":0" /> The first member of this family is the [[Kaniadakis Exponential distribution|κ-exponential distribution]] of Type I. The κ-Erlang is a κ-deformed version of the [[Erlang distribution]]. It is one example of a [[Kaniadakis distribution]].

== Characterization ==

=== Probability density function ===
The Kaniadakis ''κ''-Erlang distribution has the following [[probability density function]]:<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Kaniadakis |first=G. |date=2021-01-01 |title=New power-law tailed distributions emerging in κ-statistics (a) |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/0295-5075/133/10002 |journal=Europhysics Letters |volume=133 |issue=1 |article-number=10002 |doi=10.1209/0295-5075/133/10002 |issn=0295-5075|arxiv=2203.01743 |bibcode=2021EL....13310002K |s2cid=234144356 }}</ref>

: <math> 
f_{_{\kappa}}(x) = \frac{1}{ (n - 1)! } \prod_{m = 0}^n \left[ 1 + (2m -n)\kappa \right] x^{n - 1} \exp_\kappa(-x)
</math>

valid for <math>x \geq 0</math> and <math>n = \textrm{positive} \,\,\textrm{integer} </math>, where <math>0 \leq |\kappa| < 1</math> is the entropic index associated with the [[Kaniadakis statistics|Kaniadakis entropy]]. 

The ordinary [[Erlang distribution|Erlang Distribution]] is recovered as <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0</math>.

=== Cumulative distribution function ===
The [[Cumulative distribution function|cumulative distribution]] function of ''κ''-Erlang distribution assumes the form:<ref name=":0" />

: <math>F_\kappa(x) = \frac{1}{ (n - 1)! } \prod_{m = 0}^n \left[ 1 + (2m -n)\kappa \right] \int_0^x z^{n - 1} \exp_\kappa(-z) dz </math>

valid for <math>x \geq 0</math>, where <math>0 \leq |\kappa| < 1</math>. The cumulative [[Erlang distribution]] is recovered in the classical limit <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0</math>.

=== Survival distribution and hazard functions ===
The survival function of the ''κ''-Erlang distribution is given by:
<math display="block">S_\kappa(x) = 1 - \frac{1}{ (n - 1)! } \prod_{m = 0}^n \left[ 1 + (2m -n)\kappa \right] \int_0^x z^{n - 1} \exp_\kappa(-z) dz </math>
The survival function of the ''κ''-Erlang distribution enables the determination of hazard functions in closed form through the solution of the ''κ''-rate equation: <math display="block">\frac{ S_\kappa(x) }{ dx } = -h_\kappa S_\kappa(x) </math>where  <math>h_\kappa</math> is the hazard function.

== Family distribution ==
A family of ''κ''-distributions arises from the ''κ''-Erlang distribution, each associated with a specific value of <math>n</math>, valid for <math>x \ge 0</math> and <math>0 \leq |\kappa| < 1</math>. Such members are determined from the ''κ''-Erlang cumulative distribution, which can be rewritten as:

: <math>F_\kappa(x) = 1 - \left[ R_\kappa(x) + Q_\kappa(x) \sqrt{1 + \kappa^2 x^2} \right] \exp_\kappa(-x) </math>

where

: <math>Q_\kappa(x) = N_\kappa \sum_{m=0}^{n-3} \left( m + 1 \right) c_{m+1} x^m + \frac{N_\kappa}{1-n^2\kappa^2} x^{n-1} </math>
: <math>R_\kappa(x) = N_\kappa \sum_{m=0}^{n} c_{m} x^m </math>

with

: <math>N_\kappa = \frac{1}{ (n - 1)! } \prod_{m = 0}^n \left[ 1 + (2m -n)\kappa \right] </math>
: <math>c_n = \frac{ n\kappa^2 }{ 1 - n^2 \kappa^2} </math>
: <math>c_{n - 1} =0 </math>
: <math>c_{n - 2} = \frac{ n - 1 }{ (1 - n^2 \kappa^2) [1 - (n-2)^2\kappa^2]} </math>
: <math>c_m = \frac{ (m + 1)(m+2) }{ 1 - m^2 \kappa^2} c_{m+2} \quad \textrm{for} \quad 0 \leq m \leq n-3 </math>

=== First member ===
The first member (<math>n = 1</math>) of the ''κ''-Erlang family is the [[Kaniadakis Exponential distribution|''κ''-Exponential distribution]] of type I, in which the [[probability density function]] and the [[cumulative distribution function]] are defined as:

: <math> 
f_{_{\kappa}}(x) = (1 - \kappa^2) \exp_\kappa(-x)
</math>
: <math>F_\kappa(x) = 1-\Big(\sqrt{1+\kappa^2 x^2} + \kappa^2 x \Big)\exp_k({-x)}
</math>

=== Second member ===
The second member (<math>n = 2</math>) of the ''κ''-Erlang family has the [[probability density function]] and the [[cumulative distribution function]] defined as:

: <math> 
f_{_{\kappa}}(x) = (1 - 4\kappa^2)\,x \,\exp_\kappa(-x)
</math>
: <math>F_\kappa(x) = 1-\left(2\kappa^2 x^2 + 1 + x\sqrt{1+\kappa^2 x^2} \right) \exp_k({-x)}
</math>

=== Third member ===
The second member (<math>n = 3</math>)  has the [[probability density function]] and the [[cumulative distribution function]] defined as:

: <math> 
f_{_{\kappa}}(x) = \frac{1}{2} (1 - \kappa^2) (1 - 9\kappa^2)\,x^2 \,\exp_\kappa(-x)
</math>
: <math>F_\kappa(x) = 1-\left\{ \frac{3}{2} \kappa^2(1 - \kappa^2)x^3 + x + \left[ 1 + \frac{1}{2}(1-\kappa^2)x^2 \right] \sqrt{1+\kappa^2 x^2}\right\} \exp_\kappa(-x)
</math>

== Related distributions ==

* The [[Kaniadakis Exponential distribution|''κ''-Exponential distribution of type I]] is a particular case of the ''κ''-Erlang distribution when <math>n = 1</math>;
* A ''κ''-Erlang distribution corresponds to am ordinary exponential distribution when <math>\kappa = 0</math> and <math>n = 1</math>;
